children: Meta Platforms, the social-media and personal-AI company

, received a Wells Fargo price-target increase to $1,000 from $796, MarketWatch reported, while shares stood at $722.11 at 10.55am EST on October 9, up approximately 0.17% from the previous close. That leaves roughly 38.5% upside to the analyst's target. A big forecast. Now comes the harder part: delivering the earnings to support it.

Wells Fargo sees AI spending and legal expenses squeezing near-term profits before stronger gains emerge by 2028, according to MarketWatch. Meanwhile, Meta outlined its infrastructure approach in a discussion with infrastructure chief Santosh Janardhan, covering chip selection and the benefits of building its own data centers. The investment case hinges on whether that spending produces better advertising results, useful AI products and lower computing costs.

The valuation snapshot puts shares 16.36% below the $863.38 GF Value estimate, suggesting potential value if Meta delivers. But an estimated discount cannot pay the infrastructure bill. Owning more of the technology could improve efficiency while leaving Meta responsible for expensive execution mistakes. The $1,000 case needs evidence that AI lifts revenue or margins. More computing capacity alone will not settle that question.

title: Meta Stocks Hold Flat as Wells Fargo Sees $1,000 Path
